title: A fixed ideal power kills the stabilized annihilator
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], I ideal-sheaf data [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and H a coherent quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the recursive powers and multiplication images [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. There exist r, a quasi-coherent module T, and a monomorphism a:T -> H such that the inclusion I^r T -> T is zero, and every section s of H on every open W locally annihilated by any I^n belongs to the section range of a on W. Local annihilation means that every section b of the recursive nth power on every V <= W acts as zero on s restricted to V.

source.place: Tag 01YB, second paragraph, stabilization before the Artin-Rees argument; Tags 01PO and 01Y8.

proof.text: Construct each H_n and its monomorphic inclusion using exists_annihilator_subsheaf for the ideal-data power I^n. The affine annihilator criterion identifies its affine section range with elements annihilated by the affine ideal power.

Prove quasi-coherence by the two principal-open localization criteria. For a section on D(f), clear a denominator after mapping into H. The ideal on an affine Noetherian ring has finitely many generators; each generator kills the localized section, so clear a power of f for each and take their maximum. The resulting f-power multiple on the affine is annihilated by every generator, hence by the ideal, and lifts to H_n. Injectivity of H_n -> H cancels the map into H. The zero-localization criterion follows directly from H and injectivity. Empty generator families use exponent zero.

For n<=m the affine ideal power I(U)^m is contained in I(U)^n. The affine-annihilator formulas therefore give range(H_n(U)) contained in range(H_m(U)). Show the first inclusion composed with the cokernel of the second is zero on an affine basis and hence everywhere by separatedness. The kernel-of-cokernel image factorization gives the subobject inequality. Apply Noetherian ACC and use monotonicity below r and stabilization above r to put every H_n inside H_r.

Use the canonical isomorphism between ideal-data powers and recursive powers to equate their section ranges on every open. This converts the annihilator condition into the precise local recursive-power condition in the statement.

Every recursive-power scalar kills a section of H_r: test its image under the inclusion in H and cancel the sectionwise injective map. On affine opens the tensor sections comparison, tensor induction and quasi-coherent image formula show that the product inclusion has range generated by such scalar products. It is zero there and therefore zero everywhere by sheaf separatedness. Finally the subobject inclusion H_n <= H_r factors the actual section inclusion and gives the desired section range condition.

proof_origin.place: Stabilization part of 01YB proved in Lean. Adapts the principal-open finite-generator proof from AnnihilatorQuasicoherent with generators of the affine ideal itself, avoiding its cyclic imports.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_coherent_idealPower_stable_annihilator
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (H : X.Modules) [H.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hH : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace H) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (T : X.Modules) (a : T ⟶ H),
      Mono a ∧ T.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι r).2 T = 0 ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (W : X.Opens) (s : H.val.obj (op W)),
        (∀ (V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ W)
          (b : (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).1.val.obj (op V)),
          ((idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2.val.app (op V) b : Γ(X, V)) •
            H.val.map (homOfLE h).op s = 0) →
          s ∈ Set.range (a.app W)
